subjects.displayTitle: Resurrection: learning to recognize the Day
subjects.introduction: The Day of Resurrection has come, Bahá’u’lláh tells Ahmad, and the heedless lie in a strange sleep. Few sentences overturn expectation so completely. The trumpet, the opened graves, the balance and the bridge are not discarded but read anew: the call of a Manifestation is the trumpet, the soul that hears and acknowledges it has already crossed the bridge, and the secrets of every heart are laid bare. The Báb speaks of each revelation as the resurrection of the one before it, and of a Day whose measure of fifty thousand years is a symbol of its vastness. The Gospel of John holds a similar tension between a crossing from death to life that happens now and a summons from the tombs still to come [1]. Such a Day asks less for watching the sky than for waking up. The path leads on into the language of the Qur’an and its traditions, the imagery that clothes its warnings and promises, and the old question of how prophecy is fulfilled before eyes that do not see.
subjects.arc: Awaken perception, investigate the Day’s meanings, encounter its scriptural images, and return to accountable action.

order.why: Ask why an accomplished event remains unperceived.
Open with hearing and vision as the faculties of recognition.
shortened: Say: O people of the earth! This is the Day of hearing, for the Call hath been raised from the direction of the Throne, would ye but hear it. And this is the Day of vision, for the lights of the Countenance have shone forth from the horizon of manifestation.

order.why: Disrupt passive expectation with the image of sleep.
shortened: O Ahmad! The Day of Resurrection hath come, yet the heedless are in a strange sleep.

order.why: Hear the contrast between manifestation and doubt.
shortened: Through Him the Resurrection and its might have appeared, and the Hour and its signs have been made manifest, yet most of the people are in evident doubt.

order.why: Introduce resurrection through recognition of renewed revelation.
Follow the invitation to consult the Book of Certitude.
Consider the explicitly varied meanings and ranks of the Day.
shortened: Know that regarding what you asked about the meaning of the Day of Resurrection -- it has endless ranks in God's knowledge. Among them is the Day of Origination, the Day of Creation, the Day of Production, the Day of Bringing into Being, the Day of Formation, the Day of the Term, and the Day of the Book. In brief, every matter has its day.

order.why: Read the great duration as symbolic.
Hear the reported spiritual interpretation without ending divine bounty.
Connect successive scriptural Days with the testing of recognition.
shortened: Every manifestation before its resurrection appeareth in the subsequent manifestation - for example, the resurrection of the Gospel appeared in the twenty-third year of the revelation of the Furqan (Qur'an), and the resurrection of the Qur'an appeared in the manifestation of the Bayan, and the resurrection of the Bayan shall appear in the manifestation of Him Whom God shall make manifest, exalted be His mention.

order.why: Read the Báb’s declarations within their particular revelatory setting.
shortened: The Primal Tree hath appeared, yet ye aided it not. Say: Ye have done what God loveth not to mention. Fear ye God and weep for your souls in recompense for what your hands have wrought.
He will surely gather you together on the Day of Resurrection. This is God's decree wherein there is no doubt. Say: All shall on that Day return unto God, thy Lord.

order.why: Enter the sustained language of judgment, covenant and disclosure.
shortened: Verily ye shall have a station on the path on the Day of Resurrection where ye shall in truth be questioned. God will question His servants concerning what they do in God's religion without the judgment of truth concealed in that Book.

Verily We shall unveil the secrets on the Day of Resurrection from within yourselves in truth by truth; there shall ye bear witness unto the Most Great Remembrance through what God hath placed within you of His signs.

order.why: Identify vain imaginings as a veil.
shortened: For verily the opposers, on the Day of Presence and the Day of Manifestation, shall hang down their heads before their Lord, and thou on that day shalt be veiled from the Gate. And naught veileth thee from Him save that which thy vain imaginings have veiled thee therefrom.

order.why: Consider the multitude concealed behind that veil.
shortened: Say: The Day of Resurrection has been decreed to be fifty thousand years, and all were veiled from it. No spirit of the Bayan remained in any heart except those whom God exempted through His grace - the Letters of His Face or whomsoever He willeth from the letters of His creation.

order.why: Read living tombs as a startling image of unawareness.
Encounter the questions concerning the fulfilled catastrophe.
shortened: Has the Great Catastrophe been fulfilled? Say: Yea, by the Lord of lords! Has the Resurrection come to pass? Nay, the Self-Subsisting has appeared with the kingdom of verses. Do you see people lying prostrate? Yea, by my Lord, the Most High, the Most Glorious! Have the tree trunks been uprooted? Nay, the mountains have been scattered, by the Lord of attributes. He asked: "Where are Paradise and Hell?"

order.why: Hear the cosmic images of heavens and seas.
shortened: Say: This is the Day whereof ye were promised in the Tablets, when the heavens shall be folded up in the right hand of Power, when the earth shall be grasped by the hand of Will, and when the seas shall be set ablaze.

order.why: Read the trumpet and opened graves together.
shortened: Say: By God! This is the Day of Distinction. And what shall make thee understand what the Day of Distinction is? Woe on that Day to the deniers who deny the Day of Judgment! None denieth it save every transgressor, every sinful one. This is the Day whereon the Interlocutor of Sinai hath spoken, whereon the Trump hath been blown, those in the graves have been raised, and all who are in the heavens and on earth have swooned away, except whom God hath willed, the Mighty, the All-Praised.

order.why: Connect the trumpet with the throne of revelation.
Hear the beloved cry amid the imagery of path and balance.
Read the direct affirmation of the Hour.
shortened: One hath asked: "Hath the Resurrection come to pass?" Say: "Yea, by My All-Knowing, All-Wise Self!" "Hath the Hour arrived?" Say: "Yea, by the Lord of the Mighty Throne!"

order.why: Consider the declaration concerning the Seal of the Prophets.
shortened: Verily We have given glad-tidings unto all people that the great and blessed verse "but He is the Apostle of God and the Seal of the Prophets" hath been fulfilled in the Day when mankind shall stand before the Lord of the worlds.

order.why: Keep the claim of the oppressed speaker in its own words.
Read the gathering of all through the Manifestation.
shortened: Verily He is the One through Whom the Greater Resurrection hath come to pass and all created things have been gathered together.

order.why: Connect revival with Sinai and the covenantal question.
Move from darkness and dispersion toward gathering.
Consider the disclosure of hidden secrets.
Read the soul’s freedom and the analogy of altered taste.
shortened: When the spirit is freed from incidental limitations and earthly conditions, it traverseth all stations, and the more it is detached, the swifter, more constant and more truthful is its journey. If it be said that the human temple is, in one station, the kingdom of God, this is the truth in which there is no doubt, for the representation of all things is found and witnessed therein. Though some have called it the lesser world, yet We bear witness that it is the greater world. Its changes and variations have been and shall be due to other causes, like the change in the taste of a sick person who perceiveth bitterness in that which is sweet. The change hath not occurred in the sweetness, rather the taste hath altered.

order.why: Hold the paired images of mercy and estrangement together.
Read gathering in relation to paradise and fire.
Consider the reversal of status within the passage’s historical imagery.
shortened: O thou peerless plant in the garden of divine knowledge!

Resurrection is soul-exciting and the Day of Judgment full of blessings. The Turk turneth into a kinsman, the Arab into a foreigner and the Persian into a stranger. Distant becometh near, the deficient perfect, the learned ignorant, the poor wealthy, the rich impoverished, the mighty abased, and the abased mighty.

order.why: Retain the particular tradition concerning Friday.
Keep the Báb’s account of the beginning of resurrection distinct.
shortened: The first to prostrate before Me was Muhammad, then Ali. These are the witnesses after Him, then the Gates of Guidance - they who hastened to the Cause of their Lord, and they are the triumphant ones. Verily, the beginning of that Cause is the first Day of Resurrection when all shall be brought before God.

order.why: Consider patience within the vast measure of the Day.
Turn toward recompense for what one has earned.
Explicitly defines the Day of Resurrection as the period of the appearance of the Manifestation.
Read the balance as an account of small and great deeds.
Bring the Day into the question of one’s own deeds.
shortened: The Day which ye were promised in the Tablets hath come unto you, and every soul hath come with its deeds, though none comprehend this save those possessed of understanding.

order.why: Hear the testimony to unity, justice and the last Day.
Close with a prayer to be raised in faith and love.
shortened: O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy Name - O God, O Lord, O All-Merciful, O Inaccessible, O Holy, O He, O Mighty, O Beloved, O Subduer, O Manifest, O Single, O Unapproachable, O All-Encompassing, O Self-Subsisting, O Self-Sustaining, O Truth, O All-Knowing, O Ever-Living, O All-Powerful - to send Thy blessings upon the Letters of the Unity, and to raise me up from my resting-place on the Day of Resurrection, believing in Thee and in Thy signs, loving what Thou lovest, and abstaining from that which Thou lovest not.

questions: How does the possibility of sleeping through the Day change the meaning of spiritual expectation?
What different meanings of resurrection emerge, and how might their relationships be understood?
Which image—trumpet, balance, grave, garden, or fire—most unsettles or enlarges your reading?
How do John’s present and future statements compare with this compilation’s claims about renewed revelation?
What might it mean for judgment to disclose both hidden motives and the consequences of deeds?
How could recognizing a spiritual renewal change ordinary choices and relationships?

references.label: 1 · John 5:24–29 · Hearing, life and judgment
references.note: Read the passage’s movement from present life through hearing and believing to a coming resurrection and judgment. Compare its different temporal expressions with the compilation’s account of a Day already manifest. The Gospel’s claims about the Son and the graves should remain audible in their own setting, without assuming that every use of resurrection has an identical meaning.

subjects.displayTitle: Art and science: gifts that become work
subjects.introduction: To a young man entering an agricultural school ‘Abdu’l-Bahá wrote that his nights and days of study would be acts of worship, accepted at the threshold of the Almighty; to a painter who asked whether art was a worthy vocation He answered simply that art is worship. The claim runs deep in Bahá’u’lláh’s teaching: one of God’s names is the Fashioner, and whoever shows forth that name in skilled work is beloved of Him; knowledge is wings to a life and a ladder for ascent; the learned and the wise are the two eyes of mankind; and the sovereignty of science outlasts the sovereignty of kings. The gift carries conditions. Learning should profit the peoples of the earth rather than begin and end in words, it must be taught to girls as well as boys, and it is judged in the end by character, since arrogance can ride on achievement while love and pure intention give it another direction. Bezalel, filled with wisdom for the furnishings of the sanctuary, offers an older picture of divine gift joined to material craft and shared labour [1]. From here the way leads toward creativity in art, the mind’s power of discovery, the summons to acquire knowledge, and the high station of learning itself.
subjects.arc: Begin with work as worship, explore discovery and craftsmanship, and connect education with humility and public benefit.

order.why: Consider the reported praise of scientific achievement.
shortened: The highest praise is due to men who devote their energies to science, and the noblest center is a center wherein the sciences and arts are taught and studied. Science ever tends to the illumination of the world of humanity. It is the cause of eternal honor to man, and its sovereignty is far greater than the sovereignty of kings. The dominion of kings has an ending; the king himself may be dethroned; but the sovereignty of science is everlasting and without end.

order.why: Open with agricultural study as practical worship.
shortened: Strive as much as possible to become proficient in the science of agriculture, for in accordance with the divine teachings the acquisition of sciences and the perfection of arts are considered acts of worship. If a man engageth with all his power in the acquisition of a science or in the perfection of an art, it is as if he hath been worshipping God in churches and temples. Thus as thou enterest a school of agriculture and strivest in the acquisition of that science thou art day and night engaged in acts of worshipâ€"acts that are accepted at the threshold of the Almighty. What bounty greater than this that science should be considered as an act of worship and art as service to the Kingdom of God.

order.why: Hear the reported painter’s question and the example of drama.
Connect craftsmanship with the divine name Fashioner.
shortened: One of the names of God is the Fashioner, and He has always loved and continues to love craftsmanship. Therefore, whoever among His servants manifests this name is beloved in the presence of the Wronged One. Craftsmanship is a volume from the volumes of divine knowledge and a treasure from the treasuries of divine wisdom. This is a science with meaning, for some sciences are limited to mere words, beginning and ending with words.

order.why: Introduce arts and sciences as means of uplift.
shortened: In the third Tajalli (effulgence) of the Book of Tajalliyat (Book of Effulgences) We have mentioned: "Arts, crafts and sciences uplift the world of being, and are conducive to its exaltation. Knowledge is as wings to man's life, and a ladder for his ascent. Its acquisition is incumbent upon everyone. The knowledge of such sciences, however, should be acquired as can profit the peoples of the earth, and not those which begin with words and end with words.  Great indeed is the claim of scientists and craftsmen on the peoples of the world.

order.why: Read learning and wisdom as the eyes of humanity.
Discusses the value of medicine and knowledge serving the preservation and wellbeing of humanity.
Hear knowledge celebrated as life and light.
Consider understanding as a divine bestowal.
Explore the purposes of the faculties of perception.
shortened: First and foremost among these favors, which the Almighty hath conferred upon man, is the gift of understanding. His purpose in conferring such a gift is none other except to enable His creature to know and recognize the one true God—exalted be His glory. This gift giveth man the power to discern the truth in all things, leadeth him to that which is right, and helpeth him to discover the secrets of creation.

order.why: Read the rational soul’s discovery of hidden realities and its limits.
shortened: All the sciences, branches of learning, arts, inventions, institutions, undertakings and discoveries have resulted from the comprehension of the rational soul. These were once impenetrable secrets, hidden mysteries and unknown realities, and the rational soul gradually discovered them and brought them out of the invisible plane into the realm of the visible. This is the greatest power of comprehension in the world of nature, and the uttermost limit of its flight is to comprehend the realities, signs and properties of contingent things.

order.why: Continue with discovery as a human faculty.
Read inductive reason and the mirror of the world.
Bring questions to the scale of reason.
shortened: For in the human world there is no greater gift than reason. Reason discovers the realities of things. Reason is the standard of understanding. Therefore, weigh every question on the scale of reason. If it accords with reason, then this is what is sought; if it conflicts with reason, there is no doubt that it is mere fancy.

order.why: Keep the reported appeal to science and reason in religious conviction.
Read the historical rhetoric of discovery overcoming habitual limits.
Consider the power to discover phenomena.
shortened: The station of man is great, very great. God has created man after His own image and likeness. He has endowed him with a mighty power which is capable of discovering the mysteries of phenomena.

order.why: Hear intellect described as a great gift.
shortened: The power of the intellect is one of God's greatest gifts to men, it is the power that makes him a higher creature than the animal.

order.why: Connect intellectual light with its divine source.
shortened: It is the light of the intellect which gives us knowledge and understanding, and without this light the physical eyes would be useless.
This light of the intellect is the highest light that exists, for it is born of the Light Divine.

order.why: Join reason with the power of expression.
shortened: The greatest gifts of man are reason and eloquence of expression.

order.why: Keep the reported movement from material discovery toward spirit.
Read learning within a larger account of civilization and character.
shortened: Again, there are those famed and accomplished men of learning, possessed of praiseworthy qualities and vast erudition, who lay hold on the strong handle of the fear of God and keep to the ways of salvation. In the mirror of their minds the forms of transcendent realities are reflected, and the lamp of their inner vision derives its light from the sun of universal knowledge. They are busy by night and by day with meticulous research into such sciences as are profitable to mankind, and they devote themselves to the training of students of capacity. It is certain that to their discerning taste, the proffered treasures of kings would not compare with a single drop of the waters of knowledge, and mountains of gold and silver could not outweigh the successful solution of a difficult problem.

order.why: Consider wisdom and progress in the Forel passage.
Read the argument for knowledge within its historical vocabulary.
shortened: For knowledge is light, life, felicity, perfection and beauty, and causes the soul to draw nigh to the divine threshold. It is the honour and glory of the human realm and the greatest of God's bounties. Knowledge is identical to guidance and ignorance is the essence of error.

Happy are those who spend their days in the pursuit of knowledge, in the discovery of the secrets of the universe, and in the meticulous investigation of truth! And woe to those who content themselves with ignorance, who delight in thoughtless imitation, who have fallen into the abyss of ignorance and unawareness, and who have thus wasted their lives!

order.why: Connect learning with flourishing.
Consider which studies benefit people.
shortened: Scientific matters should be confined to what benefits people, not matters that are mere words leading only to dispute - specifically theology, mathematics, natural philosophy and material arts, so that people may benefit from them.

order.why: Retain the concrete range of mathematics and natural sciences.
Turn to the foundations laid in childhood.
shortened: O ye recipients of the favors of God! In this new and wondrous Age, the unshakable foundation is the teaching of sciences and arts. According to explicit Holy Texts, every child must be taught crafts and arts, to the degree that is needful.

order.why: Read education for both girls and boys as a major service.
shortened: This is the day in which the diffusion of sciences, the training in arts, and the instruction of children - both boys and girls - are amongst the greatest and most fundamental principles of this radiant century and this glorious age.

No greater service than this doth exist, inasmuch as the world is resplendent and illuminated by the light of the sciences and arts. Science is the light of the world; it is conducive to the joy and fervor of the people of splendor, it is life eternal, and it is everlasting glory.

order.why: Consider learning as the fruit of an educational garden.
shortened: It is my hope that thou wilt become a child of the Kingdom, wilt study arts, sciences and divine knowledge, mayest turn into a fruitful and flourishing tree in the Vineyard of God and that, through the sprinkling of the clouds of His loving providence, thou mayest appear in the utmost freshness and tender beauty.

order.why: Hear the aspiration for physical and spiritual sciences together.
shortened: 'Abdu'l-Baha is expecting to hear good news from that school; i.e. that the young fruits of the divine garden are being developed and educated in the college of realities and significances and are graduated in physical and spiritual sciences, that they are opening the eloquent tongues and are discoursing intelligently in every branch of learning so that in oratory they may become ideal magicians.

order.why: Consider organized support for arts and sciences.
shortened: And may all the friends strive that day by day it may attain greater organization and that sciences and arts may spread more abundantly.

order.why: Read the obligation to promote learning.
shortened: There are certain pillars which have been established as the unshakeable supports of the Faith of God. The mightiest of these is learning and the use of the mind, the expansion of consciousness, and insight into the realities of the universe and the hidden mysteries of Almighty God.
To promote knowledge is thus an inescapable duty imposed on every one of the friends of God.

order.why: Keep scientific attainment and teaching together.
shortened: Now as to what thou askest concerning giving up the scientific attainment in Paris for the sake of confining thy days to the delivery of this Truth, it is indeed acceptable and beloved, but if thou acquire both it would be better and more perfect, because in this new century the attainment of science, arts and belles lettres, whether divine or worldly, material or spiritual, is a matter which is acceptable before God and a duty which is incumbent upon us to accomplish.

order.why: Hear the hope for distinction that conveys blessings.
shortened: I beseech God that ye may be so highly distinguished in sciences that your fame will be noised throughout all regions and your fair name be on the lips of all enlightened people; that ye may become the means of the exaltation of the Cause of God and the exponents of the manifold blessings of the Abha Beauty.

order.why: Read the painter’s counsel concerning technical mastery and spiritual growth.
shortened: His Holiness Baha'u'llah has commanded the study of arts and crafts; that when we undertake the study of any branch of arts we must perfect ourselves in it and strive to master its technicalities and expressions but the study of art must not hinder the unfoldment of the sweet flowers of our spiritual life. One must become a complement to the other.

order.why: Consider pleasing craftsmanship amid steadfastness.
shortened: That which you sent was presented before the Throne and was honored with acceptance. God, exalted be His glory, has loved to witness pleasing crafts from His loved ones. Blessed art thou for what thou hast crafted has been presented before the face of thy Lord, the Wronged One, the Stranger.
God willing, may each of the loved ones be enabled to manifest a craft from among the crafts and be assisted in that which they have been commanded in the Book of God, the Mighty, the Wise.

order.why: Retain the reported statement about the gift of art.
shortened: All true art is a gift of the Holy Spirit."

order.why: Connect skilled practice with the spirit of service.
Read work as an expression of the worker’s qualities.
shortened: Man must work and in that work show the qualities of GOD and thus do good. His work, both material and spiritual, must show what he is. By his arts, sciences, inventions and all of his work he must show his best ability.

order.why: Locate honor in knowledge and righteous character.
shortened: The word of God which the Supreme Pen hath recorded on the fifth leaf of the Most Exalted Paradise is this: Above all else, the greatest gift and the most wondrous blessing hath ever been and will continue to be Wisdom. It is man's unfailing Protector. It aideth him and strengtheneth him. Wisdom is God's Emissary and the Revealer of His Name the Omniscient. Through it the loftiness of man's station is made manifest and evident.
In the estimation of the people of Baha man's glory lieth in his knowledge, his upright conduct, his praiseworthy character, his wisdom, and not in his nationality or rank.

order.why: Consider respect for learning freed from covetousness.
Examine the danger of intellectual arrogance.
shortened: Although to acquire the sciences and arts is the greatest glory of mankind, this is so only on condition that manis river flow into the mighty sea, and draw from Godis ancient source His inspiration. When this cometh to pass, then every teacher is as a shoreless ocean, every pupil a prodigal fountain of knowledge. If, then, the pursuit of knowledge lead to the beauty of Him Who is the Object of all Knowledge, how excellent that goal; but if not, a mere drop will perhaps shut a man off from flooding grace, for with learning cometh arrogance and pride, and it bringeth on error and indifference to God.

order.why: Read love as the fruitfulness of learning.
shortened: And every branch of learning, conjoined with the love of God, is approved and worthy of praise; but bereft of His love, learning is barren -- indeed, it bringeth on madness. Every kind of knowledge, every science, is as a tree: if the fruit of it be the love of God, then is it a blessed tree, but if not, that tree is but dried-up wood, and shall only feed the fire.

order.why: Close the linked sequence with pure intention and sustained effort.
shortened: What a heavenly potentiality God has deposited within us! What a power God has given our spirits! He has endowed us with a power to penetrate the realities of things; but we must be self-abnegating, we must have pure spirits, pure intentions, and strive with heart and soul while in the human world to attain everlasting glory.

order.why: Retain the supplied statement joining learning with justice.
Close with the supplied Einstein reflection on humility and wonder.

questions: How might a familiar activity become worship through its purpose and quality?
What do science and art disclose through their different ways of attending to reality?
How can education cultivate both technical mastery and the qualities needed to use it well?
What forms of pride can accompany learning, and what would intellectual humility look like in practice?
How does Bezalel’s particular commission illuminate or differ from the wider invitation to work in this compilation?
How could the connected subjects of creativity and discovery deepen your understanding of service?

references.label: 1 · Exodus 31:1–11 · Wisdom in craftsmanship
references.note: The Hebrew–English text describes Bezalel, Oholiab, and other skilled workers receiving wisdom for the furnishings of the sanctuary. Compare this union of divine gift, material skill, and shared labor with the compilation’s account of craftsmanship and worship. A particular sanctuary commission and a wider vocation to art, science, and service provide related but distinct frames.

subjects.displayTitle: The unschooled Manifestation: knowledge and its source
subjects.introduction: We have not entered any school, Bahá’u’lláh tells the learned; He was seated when the hand of God raised Him and silent when He was made to speak. The Báb, a young merchant, asks the just among His hearers whether He ever studied with any of their divines, and points to verses that flowed without pause of the pen as their own proof. The subject turns on a distinction between knowledge acquired and knowledge innate. The sun does not borrow its light; a lamp that has to be lit is not eternal; the tree of life bears fruit by birth and not by grafting. Yet the testimonies are human and various, and a remembered detail about the Báb’s brief schooling warns against flattening them into a single formula. John’s Gospel records the same surprise at a teacher who had never learned letters, and Jesus’ reply that His teaching came from the One who sent Him [1]. None of this disparages study; it asks how authority becomes recognisable in a life. From here the path leads to the proofs of the Manifestations of God and to the physical limitations They accept.
subjects.arc: Start with the claim of divine initiative, examine testimony and its distinctions, and ask what makes an educator authoritative.

order.why: Hear the direct address of the unlettered speaker.
Open with silence transformed into speech by divine initiative.
shortened: We have not entered any school. I was seated when the hand of thy Lord, the All-Merciful, raised Me up, and I was silent when He caused Me to speak that which draweth you nigh unto Him.

order.why: Consider unexpected knowledge emerging from ordinary livelihood.
Read the Báb’s appeal to the scope and manner of His writings.
Keep the challenge concerning youth with its answer.
Read the merchant’s declaration to the king.
Consider eloquence attributed to inspiration.
Connect the claim with the Qur’anic account of divine teaching.
Hear the distinction between customary learning and revelation.
Read the Book itself as offered proof.
Retain the Báb’s appeal to the judgment of the just.
Consider the narrative account of how writings were received.
Read the statement from Some Answered Questions about the Báb.
shortened: As for the Bab---may my soul be His sacrifice!---it was at a young age, that is, in the twenty-fifth year of His blessed life, that He arose to proclaim His Cause. Among the Shi'ihs it is universally acknowledged that He never studied in any school, nor acquired learning from any teacher. To this the people of Shiraz, each and all, bear witness.

order.why: Preserve the remembered detail of brief schooling alongside broader claims.
Make the distinction between acquired and innate knowledge explicit.
shortened: Great minds, geniuses often have an astonishing school knowledge, be it acquired by themselves (autodidactic), be it acquired through teachers and schooling, but this acquired knowledge ('ilm-i-kasbi), admirable as it is, is not to be compared with the innate knowledge ('ilm-i-ladduni) of a Prophet. Even the unlettered Prophet - see His Holiness, our Lord Muhammad, the unlettered camel-driver - has revealed in the Qur'an verses of a grammatical correctness, purity of style (fasahat) and in a language which touches the heart (balaghat), which will remain for ever the guideline, the eternally valid measure for the Arabic language.

order.why: Explore the reported images of sun, lamp and fruit tree.
shortened: The sun emanates from itself and does not draw its light from other sources. The divine teachers have the innate light; they have knowledge and understanding of all things in the universe; the rest of the world receives its light from them and through them the arts and sciences are revived in each age.
Abraham and Moses went to no school; Jesus had neither school nor master; Mohammed never had a lesson; the Bab and Baha'u'llah had no professors.
How can a lamp which has to be lighted be eternal? The divine teacher does not come to acquire knowledge, for this tree of life is a fruit tree by birth and not through grafting.

order.why: Read the reported objection to manufacturing a sun from a candle.
shortened: They do not realize that to deem him who will be the World Teacher to be in need of education by others is like trying to create a resplendent Sun by using the oil and wick of a candle.

order.why: Consider the universal Educator’s relation to human schooling.
shortened: One who is in need of the knowledge of the Professors of a university will not become the Manifestation of God. Christ was never taught by any man yet he was the universal Educator. Baha'u'llah did not study but his knowledge was immeasurable.

order.why: Read the argument concerning Moses and assistance.
shortened: A man with a stammering tongue can hardly sustain an ordinary conversation, let alone accomplish what He did! No: Were He not assisted by a divine power, He would never have been able to carry out such a mighty task.
How can a mere shepherd lay the foundation for all these branches of learning? There is no doubt that He was assisted by an extraordinary power.

order.why: Keep the account of Muhammad’s challenge to inherited rejection.
Retain the observation about prophets and writing.
Consider the reported claim about the enduring work of divine educators.
Hear Bahá’u’lláh’s declaration in the Epistle to the Son of the Wolf.
Read the corresponding appeal in the Tablet to the king.
Consider the account of Arabic eloquence.
shortened: Baha'u'llah never studied Arabic, had a teacher or tutor, or entered a school. Nevertheless His eloquence and fluency in spoken Arabic, as well as in His Arabic Tablets, would astonish the most articulate and accomplished among the Arab men of letters, and all acknowledged that in this His attainments were without peer or equal.

order.why: Read the appeal to testimony from opponents.
shortened: Another proof is that all the Persian divines and prominent leaders in Tihran know, beyond any doubt, that Baha'u'llah never attended any school, nor received any formal education, and from early childhood conducted Himself differently. Nevertheless, the divines and the learned of the East have testified to His extraordinary knowledge, wisdom, understanding, and perfections. Despite their denial and bitter enmity, they still acknowledge that Baha'u'llah was a unique and peerless Figure of the age, although they do not recognize His sublime station as do the chosen ones and the sincere.

order.why: Hear the reported recollection of difficult questions answered.
Keep the reported household scene of inquiry.
shortened: His house was always full of people - crowded. They used to come and ask questions. Notwithstanding that his holiness Baha'u'llah had never been at any school nor studied any sciences. This is certain. People of learning used to come - people of sciences - people of religion, of every sect, and he would answer their questions. People were astonished that the Blessed Beauty had never studied. Where did he get his wisdom? Where his knowledge?

order.why: Read the recipient’s own witness invoked as evidence.
shortened: Should your honor reflect upon the Cause of this servant, it would suffice. For you yourself bear witness that this servant has not acquired the outward sciences nor attended any school. Yet the waters of divine knowledge and wisdom flow from his tongue and pen in such measure that all creation is powerless to comprehend or enumerate them.

order.why: Consider knowledge flowing amid confinement.
Read rejection alongside the offered signs.
shortened: Though the clearest proofs attest the truth of His Cause; though the prophecies He, in an unmistakable language, hath made have been fulfilled; though, in spite of His not being accounted among the learned, His being unschooled and inexperienced in the disputations current among the divines, He hath rained upon men the showers of His manifold and divinely-inspired knowledge; yet, behold how this generation hath rejected His authority, and rebelled against Him!

order.why: Explore the challenge to customary religious credentials.
shortened: Wronged One hath neither associated with you and your like, nor seen your books, nor entered your classes. His headdress, His locks, and His attire all bear witness to what hath been said. Where hath fairness gone? In what place doth the embodiment of justice repose? Open your eyes, look with the eye of insight, and ponder, that ye may not be deprived of the rays of the Sun of Utterance nor be barred from the surging waves of the ocean of knowledge.
God hath manifested His Cause from a House wherein was found naught of what the divines, the jurists, the mystics and the learned possessed.

order.why: Keep the speaker’s social origin visible.
Retain the concise statement concerning schools and divines.
Read the same theme addressed to one nearby.
shortened: O thou who dwellest in My vicinity and drinketh the choice wine of My utterance! This Wronged One hath not attended schools nor engaged in formal discourse.

order.why: Consider wisdom as an ocean.
Keep the paradox of reading and writing without instruction.
Hear the distinction from those conventionally taught.
Consider the stated purpose beyond rehearsing current sciences.
shortened: Say: We have never entered any school, nor do We wish to expound in Our Tablets what the people possess and their sciences.

order.why: Read the claim’s public force.
shortened: We have not entered schools. We have come from the dawning-place of utterance with a Cause before which the hosts of the heavens and earth cannot stand.

order.why: Consider the relation of learning to revealed wisdom.
shortened: Say: We have not entered schools, yet We have sent down from the heaven of knowledge and wisdom that before which all the learning of the earth hath bowed down, as every discerning one doth testify.

order.why: Read the summons directed toward divines and rulers.
shortened: Having never attended school nor studied books of learning, through divine power and celestial might and glory, openly and without any veil, He summoned and guided the divines and rulers of the earth to the Dayspring of Revelation and the Dawning-Place of inspiration.

order.why: Hear the call to respond.
shortened: Cast aside what ye possess and take hold of that which I have commanded you, from this unlettered Youth Who calleth all to God, the One, the All-Informed."

order.why: Retain the testimony concerning reputation and learning.
Keep the reported comparison of linguistic accomplishment.
shortened: Mahomet was an Arab and wrote in Arabic - but - here on this coast - the Bab and the Blessed Perfection were not learned men: they were never taught and did not know Arabic - (the Bab was a merchant without learning) - yet they both wrote in Arabic the most wonderful choice of language and words.

order.why: Distinguish ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s reported account of His own Arabic.
shortened: All the old Baha'is know that I have never studied Arabic. I have not taken one lesson in Arabic. No one may believe this but there are still some believers living who bear testimony to this fact. Yet my Arabic, both written and spoken is the masterpiece all over the East.

order.why: Read His reported experience of answering theological questions.
Describes the astonishment caused by Baha’u’llah’s utterances despite His never having attended school.
Retain the reported description of knowledge amid tribulation.
Close with the distinct reported example of an inspired believer, not a Manifestation.
shortened: "This is also one of the most distinctive signs of the Baha'i cycle that a person who has never entered the doors of a school, who has not studied grammar and syntax sitsdown and writes such scholarly works; for example a man like Mirza Mohamad Afshar who has written such a significant book. To those who are just, there is no greater proof than this!

questions: What kinds of evidence for spiritual authority are offered beyond formal credentials?
How do the images of sun, lamp, and fruit tree shape the distinction between acquired and innate knowledge?
What changes when the reader distinguishes direct declarations, later accounts, and remembered words?
How should differing details about schooling affect the care with which this theme is stated?
What does John’s account add about the purpose of teaching and the desire for personal glory?
How can these exceptional claims be read alongside the strong encouragement to study and educate oneself?

references.label: 1 · John 7:14–18 · The source of teaching
references.note: The Gospel records surprise at Jesus’ learning and His response concerning the One who sent Him. Compare the attention to divine origin, willing practice, and freedom from self-glorification with this collection’s arguments. The comparison raises questions about recognizing authority; it does not establish identical biographical histories for different religious figures.

subjects.displayTitle: Prayer for service: making the whole person available
subjects.introduction: Assist me to gladden the hearts of Thy chosen ones, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá prays, and the prayers for service grow from that small, concrete wish into the largest of horizons: to serve the world of humanity, to guide all nations to the shores of the ocean of God’s oneness. Nothing is left out of the offering. Limbs, heart and tongue are to be strengthened; scattered affairs set in order so that teaching becomes possible; a household, a city, a whole region drawn in; words given where words fail; help asked under every condition, in prison, amid clamour, in tyranny and doubt. We are helpless and poor, the prayer admits, and Thou art the Lord of strength, and from that admission comes a strength that is shared rather than owned. Psalm 90 counts its brief days and still asks that the work of human hands be established [1], the same hope that finite lives may bear lasting fruit. Prayer of this kind turns inward dependence into outward care. From here the journey continues into service to others and to the Cause of God, and into the broader life of prayer.
subjects.arc: Begin with comfort and bodily strength, widen toward shared service, and end with enduring deeds and gratitude.

order.why: Consider service to friends as the desired gift.
shortened: O my Lord! Thou knowest me and art aware that I entertain no desire but this, seek refuge in naught else but this.
If Thou shouldst confirm me in the service of Thy friends this verily would be the most meritorious of gifts and the cause of ever abiding mercy.

order.why: Open with the concrete desire to comfort and gladden others.
Include limbs, heart and tongue in the act of service.
shortened: Strengthen, O my God, my limbs and my heart and my tongue for Thy service and Thy love and Thy praise.

order.why: Widen the horizon to humanity.
shortened: Enable us to serve the world of humanity. Make us the cause of fellowship between hearts.

order.why: Connect service with putting scattered affairs in order.
Read acknowledged weakness as an appeal for shared strength.
shortened: O Lord, our God! We are helpless; Thou art the Lord of strength and power. We are wretched; Thou art the Almighty, the All-Glorious. We are poor; Thou art the All-Possessing, the Most Generous. Graciously assist us in our servitude to Thy sacred Threshold, and aid us, through Thy strengthening grace, to worship Thee at the dawning-places of Thy praise. Enable us to diffuse Thy holy fragrances amongst Thy creatures, and strengthen our loins to serve Thee amidst Thy servants, so that we may guide all nations to Thy Most Great Name and lead all peoples to the shores of the glorious ocean of Thy oneness.

order.why: A prayer for strength and wisdom to overcome self and render service.
Hear ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s request for help in His own work.
shortened: Do thou, on my behalf, lay thy head on the sacred Threshold, and perfume brow and hair in the dust of that Door, and ask that I may be confirmed in my work; that I may, in return for His endless bounties, win, if He will, a drop out of the ocean of servitude.

order.why: Read it as the aspiration of heart and soul.
shortened: Make us successful in serving Thy friends and confirmed in servitude to Thy loved ones. This is the ultimate desire of heart and soul, this is the ultimate aspiration of conscience and being.

order.why: Hear a petition on behalf of another servant.
Join service to God with service to loved ones.
shortened: I beseech Thee by the breezes of Thy revelation, the dawning-places of Thy verses, and the sources of Thy commandments and laws, to aid me to serve Thee and to serve Thy loved ones.

order.why: Read the same connection through book and light.
shortened: I beseech Thee by Thy hidden mysteries and Thy shining lights and by Thy Most Great Book which Thou hast sent down to the peoples, to assist me in serving Thee and serving Thy loved ones.

order.why: Hear the concise petition for both forms of service.
Connect service with deeds befitting the Day.
Bring a household into the prayer.
Ask for encouragement for those who have begun.
Retain the simple prayer for another’s assistance.
Extend the prayer to a place and its surrounding region.
Read service as sowing, uniting and kindling hearts.
shortened: O my God and my Beloved! I draw near unto Thee through the sweet-scented breezes of Thy holiness which have perfumed all regions, and I beseech Thee by those sacred and attracted realities which have been stamped with the signs of Thy bounty from every direction, that Thou wouldst assist this servant of Thine to exalt Thy Word, to shed abroad Thy lights, to cause Thy seed to grow, to promulgate Thy Cause, to unite Thy loved ones, to gather together Thy chosen ones, to kindle the fire of Thy love in the hearts of Thy faithful ones, and to intoxicate Thy loved ones with the wine of the Covenant.

order.why: Turn to the gift of utterance.
shortened: Bestow the power of utterance that they may engage in Thy praise and be protected under the shadow of Thy grace.

order.why: Read martial images within disputation, proof and evidence.
shortened: O Lord! Make them Thy manifest signs in Thy lands, Thy waving banners over the heads of Thy servants, Thine effective arrows in the breasts of Thine enemies, Thy drawn and gleaming swords in the battlefields of disputation with Thy foes. Loose their tongues in Thy remembrance and praise, cause them to speak with Thy proof and evidence, make them proofs of the Day of Thy Manifestation and missives of Thy Kingdom, and grant them a true mention among those who come after.

order.why: Connect assistance with wisdom and utterance.
shortened: O Lord! Thou seest me clinging unto Thee and detached from all else besides Thee. I beseech Thee to assist me to serve Thy Cause and to arise to aid it through the hosts of wisdom and utterance.

order.why: Consider becoming a visible sign of love.
shortened: Lord! Make me a sign of Thy love and a standard of Thy mention and a banner waving in the highest horizon and fluttering in the Abha Kingdom.

order.why: Read trust, remembrance and service together.
shortened: Say: Glory be to Thee, O my God! I am he who has turned to Thee and placed his trust in Thee. I beseech Thee by Thy Name through which the ocean of Thy utterance surged and the breezes of Thy knowledge were stirred, to make me successful in serving Thy Cause and assisted in Thy remembrance and praise.

order.why: Hear the petition addressed to the Lord of immortality.
Read the appeal through bounty and inheritance.
Keep the concentrated request for aid.
Consider the movement from asking to arising.
shortened: I beseech Thee, O Lord of the worlds, by Thy Most Great Name through which Thou hast subdued the hearts of the nations, to aid me to arise to serve Thy Cause.

order.why: Locate service among the servants of God.
shortened: O Lord! Aid me to serve Thee amongst Thy servants and to praise Thee amidst Thy creation. Then ordain for me that which befitteth the heaven of Thy generosity and bounty, and the clouds of Thy grace and favors.

order.why: Bring remembrance, praise and service together.
shortened: I beseech Thee, O Lord of eternity and Creator of nations, by Thy Most Great Name, to make me successful in remembering Thee and praising Thee and serving Thy Cause.

order.why: Hear the request to serve at all times.
shortened: I beseech Thee by Thy greatness and sovereignty to assist me through the means of the heavens and earth that I may be occupied at all times in Thy service and speaking in Thy remembrance.

order.why: Connect illuminated sight and hearing with action.
Read strength of body with unity of hearts and reunion.
shortened: I beseech Thee by Thy Name through which Thou didst knit together the hearts of Thy loved ones, didst make known unto them Thy path, and didst teach them that which would draw them nigh unto Thee in Thy days, that Thou mayest ordain that I, under all conditions, be attracted by Thy verses, be severed from all save Thee, and cling tenaciously to Thy strong cord. O Lord! Strengthen my frame for the service of Thy Cause, illumine mine eyes with the light of beholding Thee, and then throw open before the faces of Thy servants the gates of reunion with Thee.

order.why: Consider steadfast service amid gratitude for guidance.
shortened: Say: My God, my God! Praise be to Thee for having made me to know Thee and guided me and caused me to hear. I beseech Thee by Thy Tablet and Thine ink, and by the love of Thy chosen ones, and by the enkindlement of the hearts of Thy sincere ones, and by the patience of the Dawning-Places of Thy dignity, to make me in all circumstances steadfast in Thy service and circling round Thy will.

order.why: Read steadfastness through the image of imprisonment.
shortened: I beseech Thee by Thy imprisonment which Thou hast made the seat of Thy throne and wherein Thy call was raised amongst Thy creation, to make me firm, steadfast and unwavering in Thy love and in service to Thy Cause.

order.why: Hear the desire for presence and firmness.
shortened: I beseech Thee, O Ocean of Light, by the lights of Thy countenance, the manifestations of Thy grandeur and might, and the revelations of Thy power and sovereignty, to ordain for me the reward of attaining Thy presence. Then make me a champion of Thy Cause and steadfast in Thy service.

order.why: Face doubts and tyranny without abandoning service.
shortened: I beseech Thee by the lights of Thy countenance to assist me in serving Thy Cause in such wise that the doubts of Thine enemies and the signs of the tyrants among Thy creatures shall not hold me back.

order.why: Read the prayer for perseverance amid clamor.
shortened: O Lord! I implore Thee by the breathings of Thy revelation and the manifestations of Thy grandeur, and by Thy Name through which Thou hast subdued the world, to aid me to serve Thy Cause in such wise that the clamor of Thy creatures and the might of those who have denied Thy signs may not deter me.

order.why: Keep the petition within its setting of opposition.
Consider the intensity of detachment in this prayer.
shortened: Therefore turn thy face to the Most Glorious Kingdom and seek assistance from the Most Exalted Realm, saying:

O Pure God! Grant confirmation and bestow success, that we may forget both stranger and kin, remain silent from every mention, and be moved to ecstasy by the breezes wafting from Thy sanctified gardens.

order.why: Read steadfastness with praise and testimony.
Hold this life and the world to come together.
Hear the brief appeal to the gracious Lord.
Read service under every condition.
shortened: I beseech Thee to assist me under all conditions to serve Thy Cause.

order.why: Connect action with mercy and tranquility.
shortened: I beseech Thee to make me one of those who aid Thy Cause, who arise to serve Thee, who rest beneath the canopy of Thy mercy, and who are tranquil through the lights of the Sun of Thy Beauty.

order.why: Ask for nearness that issues in service.
Join service with acknowledgment of the Book.
shortened: I moreover beseech Thee, O my God, to aid me in serving Thy Cause and in acknowledging that which hath been sent down in Thy Book.

order.why: Read remembrance and conduct together.
shortened: Say: O Lord of the world and Creator of the nations! I beseech Thee by Thy Most Great Name to make me, in all conditions, a servant of Thy Cause, a helper of Thy Faith, one who remembereth Thy Name, one who uttereth that which Thou hast sent down through Thy sovereignty, and one who acteth according to that which hath been inscribed in Thy Book.

order.why: Consider a lifetime of action and remembrance.
Hear the desire for service whose remembrance endures.
Read the prayer for another’s affairs, strength and reliance.
shortened: O Lord, O Lord! Ordain for him every good that Thou hast ordained for Thy loved ones, strengthen his loins for Thy service, make his affairs easy through Thy bounty and mercy, and make him a sign of Thy unity amongst Thy creation, speaking Thy praise, bowing before Thy threshold, relying upon Thee, and clinging to the hem of Thy grandeur.

order.why: Turn from petition to gratitude for being enabled.
shortened: Say: My God, my God! Praise be unto Thee for having enabled me to serve Thee, wherein I have taken up, in Thy vicinity, a station and place for Thy remembrance, Thy praise, and that which Thou hast commanded me in Thy days.

order.why: Close with deeds that convey acceptance and good pleasure.

questions: Which concrete need named in these prayers most closely touches your own experience of service?
How might praying for strength differ from seeking control over outcomes?
What does including the body, tongue, heart, household, and daily affairs reveal about the scope of devotion?
How do the prayers connect service to God with care for particular people and humanity?
What does Psalm 90’s awareness of limited time add to the desire for enduring work?
What act of comfort, encouragement, or practical assistance could give expression to a prayer you have read?

references.label: 1 · Psalm 90:12–17 · The work of our hands
references.note: The psalm moves from numbered days and suffering toward mercy, gladness, and the establishment of human work. Compare its petition with prayers for strength and steadfastness here. The shared concern is how finite lives may bear lasting fruit; the psalm’s particular language of lament should be heard alongside the compilation’s varied tones of praise and service.

subjects.displayTitle: Teaching oneself: becoming answerable to one’s words
subjects.introduction: Whoever wishes to deliver the Cause to others, Bahá’u’lláh says, must first deliver it to himself; those who enjoin righteousness and forget their own selves are like a lamp that gives light to servants while consuming itself. Teaching oneself is the answerability this image demands. It begins with testing one’s knowledge in practice, continues in conduct watched by everyone, and reaches into study of the Writings and of history, learning a language, caring for the sick, memorizing prayers, and finding in one’s own being the attraction and prayerful attitude without which words do not carry. Preparation never quite ends before service begins, for ‘Abdu’l-Bahá observes that our own heart is opened when we teach the heart of a listener. The Dhammapada likewise asks that one establish oneself in what is proper before instructing others, within its own discipline of training [1]. After prayer and meditation, Shoghi Effendi reminds us, comes action and perseverance. The road continues into knowledge of self, the spiritual prerequisites of teaching, and the enkindlement that turns understanding into a flame.
subjects.arc: Begin with integrity, develop practical and spiritual preparation, and return to learning through service.

order.why: Open with the lamp that lights others while consuming itself.
shortened: Whosoever among you desireth to deliver the Cause of his Lord, it behooveth him first to deliver it unto himself, then unto the people, that his words may attract the hearts of the hearers. Without this, his words will never influence the hearts of the seekers. Beware, O people, lest ye be of them who enjoin righteousness upon others but forget their own selves.
Their likeness in the sight of God is as a lamp from which servants receive light while it consumeth itself and becometh of those that are consumed.

order.why: Test knowledge through practical application.
Read the reported call to begin with one’s own education.
shortened: "Man must strive first to educate and train his own self - thus he may obtain unlimited capacity; then starts in the education of others.

order.why: Introduce the reciprocal learning that teaching can bring.
Connect teaching with deeds and conduct.
shortened: The friends of God must teach by deeds and conduct so that all will testify that verily their behavior and manner is a reflection of the heaven above.

order.why: Explains why a spiritual teacher must first put the teachings into practice.
Consider what observers learn from behavior.
shortened: All the people of the world look at us to see how we act; what our characteristics are; what our attributes are; what our mode of procedure is. They all look toward us, and we must act in such wise that we may not be the cause of the degradation of the Cause of God.

order.why: Read character and the avoidance of harm together.
Put public benefit before selfish desire.
shortened: Cling ye to the hem of virtue, and hold fast to the cord of trustworthiness and piety. Concern yourselves with the things that benefit mankind, and not with your corrupt and selfish desires. O ye followers of this Wronged One! Ye are the shepherds of mankind; liberate ye your flocks from the wolves of evil passions and desires, and adorn them with the ornament of the fear of God.

order.why: Ground service in mercy and love for humanity.
shortened: We must partake of the bounty and grace of the Lord, for the Bab has admonished us to arise in service to the Cause of God, to be absolutely severed from all else save God during the day of the Blessed Perfection, Baha'u'llah, to be completely attracted by the love of Baha'u'llah, to love all humanity for His sake, to be lenient and merciful to all for Him and to upbuild the oneness of the world of humanity.

order.why: Consider gentleness and assistance in encounters with others.
shortened: We must associate with all humanity in gentleness and kindliness. We must love all with love of the heart. Some are ignorant; they must be trained and educated. One is sick; he must be healed. Another is as a child; we must assist him to attain maturity.

order.why: Read the reported example of Christ serving the disciples.
shortened: "He brought about the Lord's Supper, and served the diciples in order to teach them that they must also serve others. This was His example to them.

order.why: Consider the inward state of attraction and prayer.
shortened: To conclude: We will say that he who wishes to teach must first find himself in the right state, to-wit,-he must discover in his own being the sense of attraction and the prayerful attitude, and by his attention to the Focal Point, will he be able to teach.

order.why: Connect perseverance with humility and restraint.
shortened: Have thou the utmost resolution and perseverance and with absolute humility and submission live among the Maidservants of the Merciful, so thou mayest always be silent and whenever you open your lips it must be to guide the capable souls, so that they may enter the Divine Religion and receive a share from the inexhaustible bounties.

order.why: Read the effect of an enkindled heart.
Consider the images of birds flying and fish swimming.
shortened: If they be birds of the meadow of divine knowledge, they must needs spread their wings and take flight unto the branches of the gardens of oneness. And if they be fish of the ocean of love, they must needs move and swim therein.

order.why: Read purposeful effort through its spiritual fruits.
Join steadfastness with wisdom and utterance.
Honor independent understanding and the capacity to explain.
Turn toward deliberate study of proofs.
shortened: Receive proofs and evidence from Mirza Abul Fazl so that thou wilt be armed with convincing proofs and sufficient argument to break down the ranks of denial, pride and ignorance.

order.why: Read the reported counsel joining care for the sick with study.
Include the practical work of learning English.
shortened: And you yourself must make the utmost effort to advance in the English language, both speaking and writing, for it will be much needed in the future.

order.why: Consider organized preparation of young teachers.
Hear the call to increase study classes.
Value education and the advancement of knowledge.
shortened: Among the most excellent services is the education and training of children and the promotion of various branches of knowledge and sciences. Now, praise be to God, you are making a mighty effort and great endeavor in this service.

order.why: Keep the concrete instructions for teaching children.
Read the hope that students become teachers.
shortened: That is, the perfect human must engage in educating and teaching all. Therefore I hope that the students of that teacher will progress in all ranks and become occupied with teaching.

order.why: Consider learning that bears the fruit of further service.
shortened: Among its fruits is that souls are being taught and instructed, and being educated under the blessed tree, they become familiar with the holy fragrances and strive to diffuse the divine breaths.

order.why: Place education within the account of a divine Educator.
Read the reported personal instruction through words and deeds.
shortened: I will not be far from thee for one second, I did not bring thee with me without a good reason nor have I kept thee so long without a cause. Be thou not grieved. I am thy instructor. I have educated thee in my own college. Thou art my student. Adorn thyself with my words, deeds, morals, manners.

order.why: Retain the brief affirmation of prior training.
shortened: Even so must you be, for I have trained you. You are the candle which I have lighted with my own hands.

order.why: Consider preparation to follow examples of service.
Hear the reported invitation for learners to begin their own songs.
shortened: I have done my part. I have sung my songs and have played almost every tune. Now it is your turn. For awhile I must sit silent ever straining my ears to hear your anthems of praise.

order.why: Read the particular prayer for those being educated.
shortened: Supplicate God that thou mayest make the young women of that tribe handmaidens of the threshold of the Mighty Lord, so that, being nurtured in the embrace of that handmaiden of God's training, they may become near to the threshold of the All-Glorious and day and night may loose their tongues in glorification and praise, and arise in thanksgiving for the bounty of the All-Merciful.

order.why: Remember the person who helped another find guidance.
shortened: Thank thou God that thou wert assisted in meeting Reverend Albert Vail and he became the cause of thy guidance. Thou wert thirsty and he suffered thee to drink the water of life. Thou wert a seeker; he caused thee to listen to the call of the Kingdom. He became the cause of thy illumination and spirituality.

order.why: Consider patient correspondence in a difficult relationship.
Read confidentiality as care for the person being approached.
shortened: Similarly, when anyone teaches another soul, keep it concealed and absolutely never disclose it, especially regarding prominent persons--the distinguished and eminent ones must be kept completely confidential. Now many important persons desire to enter under the shadow of Truth, but they fear exposure and fame. If they know they will remain concealed and protected, they will successively turn to the Faith. Consider this matter very important.

order.why: Keep the reported counsel concerning quiet material support.
Consider movement and encounters across places.
Read the aspiration to awaken understanding.
shortened: You must engage in the diffusion of the Fragrances of God, so that ye may impart life to the worlds, illumine the dark regions, confer new existence upon these mouldering, dead bodies, make intelligent and mindful these negligent hearts.

order.why: Retain the particular appeal to greater teaching effort.
shortened: If the friends of God in America were each engaged in teaching the Cause of God like the friends in Iran, by now they would have guided several million souls and joy and gladness would have been attained by all.

order.why: Keep the reported example concerning spiritual ripening.
Read the reported royal anecdote in its own historical wording.
Retain the reminder of earlier counsels on conduct.
Keep the warning about harm arising from local affairs.
Read the wish to repair what has been lost.
Close the linked sequence with a prayer that access to verses bear fitting fruit.
Retain the supplied program of careful study and unbiased inquiry.
shortened: Those who participate in such a campaign, whether in an organizing capacity, or as workers to whose care the execution of the task itself has been committed, must, as an essential preliminary to the discharge of their duties, thoroughly familiarize themselves with the various aspects of the history and teachings of their Faith. In their efforts to achieve this purpose they must study for themselves, conscientiously and painstakingly, the literature of their Faith, delve into its teachings, assimilate its laws and principles, ponder its admonitions, tenets and purposes, commit to memory certain of its exhortations and prayers, master the essentials of its administration, and keep abreast of its current affairs and latest developments.

order.why: Read the supplied guidance on understanding and inspiration.
Include the supplied invitation to wider historical and social knowledge.
Connect study with informed attention to world conditions.
Read the supplied counsel on learning while actively teaching.
Close with the supplied movement from study and meditation to persevering action.
shortened: The beloved Guardian has stressed over and over again, that to effectively teach the Faith, the individual must study deeply, the Divine Word, imbibe Its life-giving waters, and feast upon Its glorious teachings. He should then meditate on the import of the Word, and finding its spiritual depths, pray for guidance and assistance. But most important, after prayer is action. After one has prayed and meditated, he must arise, relying fully on the guidance and confirmation of Baha'u'llah, to teach His Faith. Perseverance in action is essential, just as wisdom and audacity are necessary for effective teaching.

questions: What does the consuming lamp reveal about the difference between conveying true words and living by them?
How can one begin serving while continuing to acknowledge the need for further learning?
Which practical preparations in the collection could strengthen your ability to listen and communicate?
How do confidentiality, gentleness, and quiet assistance affect the relationship between teacher and learner?
How does the Dhammapada’s discipline of personal conduct compare with the collection’s account of prayer and divine assistance?
What could help a group reflect honestly on how teaching changes its own members?

references.label: 1 · Dhammapada 158–160, 165 · Practising what one teaches
references.note: In Acharya Buddharakkhita’s translation, these verses connect instruction with personal discipline and responsibility for purification. Compare their demand for congruence between conduct and teaching with Bahá’u’lláh’s lamp image. Keep the Buddhist account of training distinct from the compilation’s language of revelation, prayer, and divine confirmation.

subjects.displayTitle: Translating sacred writings: fidelity, access and living meaning
subjects.introduction: Before any word is carried into another tongue, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asks that it be carried into conduct, so that a life becomes the clearest rendering of the teachings. On the page, He counted translation among the hardest of arts. However eloquent, it can never equal words that issued from the Source of revelation, yet it lets those without Arabic or Persian catch the fragrance of inner meanings. He asked for committees in which masters of the original and gifted writers of the new language would labour side by side, so that sense is kept and the music of the original is not lost. He also weighed timing with care, advising that the Bayán await the spread of the Kitáb-i-Aqdas so that its abrogated laws would not be mistaken for the foundation of the Faith. Paul, writing to the Corinthians, likewise asked what good speech can do for listeners who cannot understand it [1]. The work leads naturally to the preservation and authentication of sacred texts, and to the patient labour of ordering and transcribing them for every people.
subjects.arc: Begin with lived meaning, examine the translator’s art and shared labor, and consider historical choices about access and publication.

order.why: Open with deeds as the real translation of meaning.
shortened: Act in accordance with the teachings of Baha'u'llah. All His Books will be translated. Now is the time for you to live in accordance with His words. Let your deeds be the real translation of their meaning.

order.why: Introduce the demanding relation between original and translation.
Read the detailed account of collaborative style and fidelity.
shortened: But afterward, if thou desirest to get the translation of a Tablet from the Blessed Writings, it must be translated by a committee of two Persian translators together with two competent English writers. The Persians should translate, and the writers mould the significance into profound, musical and perfect cast of style in English, and in such wise that the musical sweetness of the original Persian may not be lost.

In brief, translation is one of the most difficult arts. In both Persian and English utmost proficiency is necessary, that the translator be a writer and use as the vehicle of expression great eloquence and fluency of tongue.

order.why: Consider the effects of knowing the original languages.
Keep the counsel concerning the Hidden Words’ original wording.
Retain the reported emphasis on comprehending meaning and context.
shortened: The Faith of God has not penetrated Paris and the fire of the love of God has not enkindled her people to the depth it should. Of certainty, there is wisdom in this. One reason is that, so far, a competent translator has not been found who not only can speak, but also has a thorough command of the language. Sometimes, a translation is better than the original. A translator must fully comprehend the meaning [and the context] of the words.

order.why: Read the call for skilled committees and wide circulation.
Consider the limits of solitary translation.
Explore the range of expertise envisaged for collaboration.
shortened: The translation of the Surat-ul-Hykl is of the utmost difficulty. It must be translated by a committee who are exceedingly efficient both in Persian and English, exercising the closest and most minute attention. Otherwise the text would not become intelligible.

Translations will be made by a committee composed of two most erudite Persians and two learned Americans, all of them having the utmost proficiency in both languages and possessing a certain knowledge of sciences and arts. Then others from among the scholars and thinkers must assist.

order.why: Read the practical provision for individual work when a committee is unavailable.
Keep the particular challenge of the Súriy-i-Haykal.
Hear the reported assessment of early translations.
Read the concise reported counsel on expertise.
Include the reported discipline of daily translation practice.
Turn toward sustained language learning.
shortened: O maid-servant of God! Study Persian and acquire it more day by day, for by the study of this language great and boundless results are obtained.

order.why: Join learning Persian with the work of translating.
Read study as preparation to assist other readers.
Include fluency, character and steadiness in preparation.
Consider the aspiration to literary skill in service.
shortened: God willing, you will become an eloquent translator in that language, and an incomparable writer, dictator, poet and man of letters, so that you may arise to serve the Truth and stand in servitude at the threshold of the Divine Unity.

order.why: Read the standard of expression sought for an Arabic translation.
Keep the particular provision for refining Ottoman Turkish.
Notice a woman’s contribution to beautiful verse translation.
Hear the reported encouragement offered to a translator.
shortened: Go, and eat this candy. Rest assured, the Blessed Perfection will enable you to translate the Arabic into English. Rest assured that as time goes on you will be assisted to translate from the Arabic much more easily than from the Persian.

order.why: Acknowledge the effort made by another translator.
shortened: O dear daughter! Your letter arrived and it became known that you have exerted the utmost effort in translating some of the utterances.

order.why: Read the enduring value attributed to an early translator’s service.
shortened: You are the first person who translated some of the Tablets and words of the Ancient Beauty and became the cause of the unveiling of truth. This virtue will remain forever established among the Baha'is and will not be forgotten throughout centuries and ages. Be assured that it will be inscribed in golden letters in future centuries and will spread far and wide, and this is fitting.

order.why: Connect translation with access for new audiences.
Keep the invitation to translate the Hidden Words and Some Answered Questions into Russian.
Read another Russian proposal with its condition of avoiding harm.
Consider circulation of a translation of the Book of Certitude.
Read the invitation to disseminate Tablets of counsel.
shortened: The Ishraqat, Tajalliyat, Kalimat, Bisharat, and Tarazat - such Tablets which consist of counsels and exhortations - should certainly be translated and disseminated.

order.why: Keep the reported proposal for shorter writings and accounts.
shortened: He said:-
"Translate the hidden words, the words of Paradise, Tajalleyat, Tarazat, the Baha'i proof[s] and other small pamphlets containing short historical accounts."

order.why: Read the particular program for Hindi translation.
Consider staged translation with attention to the audience.
Keep the particular provision concerning Gujarati readers.
Recognize the Esperanto translation of the Hidden Words.
Read the permission for talks and Tablets in Esperanto.
Encourages translation and publication of important Tablets in Esperanto.
Consider the interruption of Danish publication by war.
shortened: You had written that you had translated several treatises and tablets into Danish and sent them to Europe during the days of the war, but no word has yet been received about them. Since it was wartime, therefore the response from Europe was delayed. Now that war has been transformed into peace, it is hoped that the translation of those tablets and treatises will be published in Denmark.

order.why: Notice the practical limitation of insufficient German translations.
shortened: Praise be to God that the horizon of Germany is illuminated with the effulgence of the Sun of Ya Baha El Abha.
However, the work is difficult because the Divine Tablets are not yet sufficiently translated into the German language.

order.why: Read collaboration with the person responsible for a book.
Consider friends working together to print and translate.
shortened: Together with a group of friends you have undertaken the printing and translation of heavenly treatises and are striving to spread the divine fragrances so that the banner of clear verses may wave over the mountains and hills of that land. I beseech God to grant great success and make you a clear standard.

order.why: Keep the request for originals alongside translations.
Read practical limits on translators and the proposed choice of texts.
shortened: Regarding the Tablets with translation that you wrote should be sent from here - we have absolutely no translator here who can translate even one line of the Sacred Writings.

Therefore, whatever Sacred Writings are suitable to Western tastes - those that are all about universal peace and wellbeing, love and faithfulness toward all human beings, truthfulness and reconciliation and friendship between all peoples, absence of corruption, accord and unity, and the way and conduct of the people of God - have those Tablets translated in Tehran through skilled translators with perfect eloquence and excellence and in the finest style, and then print them.

order.why: Hear the reported concern about incomplete access to meaning.
shortened: Yet there were souls who were gladdened by the glad-tidings of God and attracted by the fragrances of God. Had they known Persian and understood Arabic, they would have been greatly moved. Nor were the means provided for these Tablets to be properly translated---a complete translation.

order.why: Keep the rhetorical challenge concerning distribution in its historical setting.
Read the particular advice concerning explanation and readers’ readiness.
shortened: Regarding what you wrote about translating and publishing the divine Tablets, this is not advisable at present, for it would slacken the people's thirst. First souls must be made thirsty, then the sweet and flowing water be offered. If the sacred writings were now translated, published and distributed, everyone who obtained a Tablet would be content with reading it and say, "I am now familiar with the foundations of this community and need investigate no further." Yet the Tablets must be expounded by an expounder - that is, the expounder must first establish the foundation, and after presenting the proofs, then recite a Tablet; only then will it have effect.

order.why: Consider why the Bayán’s publication is related to the Aqdas and abrogated laws.
shortened: As regards the translation and publication of the Bayan, there are laws in the Bayan which have been abrogated by the Kitab-i-Aqdas and the Baha'is are bound by the laws of the Kitab-i-Aqdas. Were the Bayan to be published and translated, the peoples of the other countries -- and indeed even the Persians -- would think that the basis of the religion of the Baha'is was those severe laws which are found in the Bayan. Whereas according to the explicit text of the Kitab-i-Aqdas those laws are not applicable.

Therefore, the Bayan must be published in all parts and corners of the world after the publication of the Kitab-i-Aqdas, so that readers may know that those severe laws have been abrogated and canceled.

order.why: Retain the historical reported account of the Aqdas’s future translation.
Keep the differing advice concerning versions of Some Answered Questions.
Read the proposal to seek permission for printing.
shortened: O herald of the Covenant! Regarding what you wrote about printing the Writings in the government press, a response was previously sent to the chief of photographers and has surely arrived by now. If it is agreeable and if the Hands of the Cause of God deem it advisable, it may be submitted with utmost wisdom to His Imperial Majesty that some of Blessed Beauty's Writings have been requested from foreign countries to be printed together with their translations and sent to foreign lands, including Ishraqat and Tajalliyat. Since there are many seekers in Europe, great benefits would result if permission for printing is granted.

order.why: Consider another historically situated request for official permission.
Retain the expectation of a future opening for circulation.
Read the growing availability of translations and talks.
Close with the prayer’s image of a portion for every people.
shortened: Thou hast endowed every hour of these days with a special virtue, inscrutable to all except Thee, Whose knowledge embraceth all created things. Thou hast, also, assigned unto every soul a portion of this virtue in accordance with the Tablet of Thy decree and the Scriptures of Thine irrevocable judgment. Every leaf of these Books and Scriptures Thou hast, moreover, alloted to each one of the peoples and kindreds of the earth.

questions: What forms of fidelity matter besides reproducing individual words?
How might different kinds of expertise help a translation preserve both meaning and literary force?
What can readers learn by distinguishing historical advice to particular recipients from a general principle?
How do preservation, authentication, and awareness of changing laws affect responsible translation?
What does Paul’s concern for shared understanding add, and where does his setting differ from the translation of scripture?
How could study of a translated text become a change in conduct without overlooking the care owed to its wording?

references.label: 1 · 1 Corinthians 14:6–19 · Speech that can be understood
references.note: Paul asks how speech can benefit a congregation when listeners cannot understand it, and relates spirit, understanding, and the ability to join in thanks. Compare this concern with the compilation’s attention to eloquence and access to meaning. Interpreting tongues in worship is a different task from translating a written scripture, so the connection lies in responsibility to the listener rather than an identical translation method.
